projection.statement: Assess technical correctness, whether claims follow from evidence, method appropriateness, and the quality of proofs or experimental design.
Assess whether the submission is clearly written and well structured, easy to follow, appropriately positioned against prior work, and sufficiently specified for expert reproduction.
Assess whether the paper addresses an important or relevant problem, advances understanding, capabilities, or practice in machine learning, or could influence future research or applications.
Assess new insights, tasks, methods, theory, data, or perspectives, while allowing combinations of existing techniques with well-articulated reasoning and new understanding of existing methods.
Assess whether the paper adequately discusses limitations and potential negative societal impact.
Assess whether ethical issues should be flagged for ethics review and require a detailed explanation.

sections.extracted_fact: The ICML 2026 main-track overall recommendation is an ordered six-point scale from Strong Reject to Strong Accept.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form Instructions > Overall Recommendation > track heading
verbatim_excerpts.text: Main Track Reviewer Form Instructions

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Overall Recommendation > heading
verbatim_excerpts.text: Overall Recommendation

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Overall Recommendation > 6
verbatim_excerpts.text: 6: Strong Accept: Technically flawless paper with exceptional impact on one or more areas of AI, with strong evaluation, reproducibility, and resources, and no unaddressed ethical considerations.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Overall Recommendation > 5
verbatim_excerpts.text: 5: Accept: Technically solid paper, with high impact on at least one sub-area of AI or moderate-to-high impact on more than one area of AI, with good-to-excellent evaluation, resources, reproducibility, and no unaddressed ethical considerations.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Overall Recommendation > 4
verbatim_excerpts.text: 4: Weak accept: Technically solid paper that advances at least one sub-area of AI, with a contribution that others are likely to build on, but with some weaknesses that limit its impact (e.g., limited evaluation). Please use sparingly.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Overall Recommendation > 3
verbatim_excerpts.text: 3: Weak reject: A paper with clear merits, but also some weaknesses, which overall outweigh the merits. Papers in this category require revisions before they can be meaningfully built upon by others. Please use sparingly.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Overall Recommendation > 2
verbatim_excerpts.text: 2: Reject: For instance, a paper with technical flaws, weak evaluation, inadequate reproducibility, incompletely addressed ethical considerations, or writing so poor that it is not possible to understand its key claims.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Overall Recommendation > 1
verbatim_excerpts.text: 1: Strong Reject: For instance, a paper with well-known results, unaddressed ethical considerations, or a poorly written paper where it is impossible to tell what the nature of its contribution is.

sections.extracted_fact: The ICML 2026 reviewer confidence field is an ordered five-point scale about certainty in the assessment.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form Instructions > Confidence > track heading
verbatim_excerpts.text: Main Track Reviewer Form Instructions

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Confidence > heading
verbatim_excerpts.text: Please provide a "confidence score" for your assessment of this submission

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Confidence > 5
verbatim_excerpts.text: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Confidence > 4
verbatim_excerpts.text: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Confidence > 3
verbatim_excerpts.text: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Confidence > 2
verbatim_excerpts.text: 2: You are willing to defend your assessment, but it is quite likely that you did not understand the central parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Confidence > 1
verbatim_excerpts.text: 1: Your assessment is an educated guess. The submission is not in your area, or the submission was difficult to understand. Math/other details were not carefully checked.

sections.extracted_fact: After rebuttal, the reviewer explains the final recommendation and how the paper and rebuttal affected it.

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form Instructions > Final Justification > track heading
verbatim_excerpts.text: Main Track Reviewer Form Instructions

verbatim_excerpts.source_locator: Main Track Reviewer Form > Final Justification (Post-Rebuttal)
verbatim_excerpts.text:
Final Justification (Post-Rebuttal)
Please explain your final recommendation, taking into account both the paper and the authors’ rebuttal. Summarize how you weighed the strengths and weaknesses across dimensions such as soundness, originality, significance, and clarity. Importantly, please indicate whether the rebuttal addressed your main concerns, changed your evaluation, or reinforced your prior assessment.
